strategy_title: Autotune with fixed grid causes instruction count doubling
strategy_description: Adding @triton.autotune improved occupancy (55.7%→75.4%) and reduced no-eligible-warp cycles (71.4%→54.7%), but the grid lambda was not updated to use meta['XBLOCK']/meta['YBLOCK'] — the launch still used the hardcoded grid=(cdiv(xnumel,128), cdiv(ynumel,8)). When autotune selected XBLOCK=256/YBLOCK=8, the fixed grid over-partitioned work, doubling executed instructions (771K→1511K) and increasing duration from 5.79µs to 6.66µs. The structural anti-pattern is adding @triton.autotune without simultaneously converting the grid to a meta-lambda, causing the selected tile size to be ignored at launch while still paying the overhead of larger blocks.
applicable_when: Any Triton kernel where @triton.autotune is added to vary tile sizes (XBLOCK, YBLOCK, BLOCK_SIZE, etc.)
do_not_apply_when: Grid is already a meta-lambda; or tile sizes are not being autotuned (fixed config only)
framework_notes: Triton-specific: when @triton.autotune varies constexpr tile parameters, the grid must be a callable lambda meta: (...) that reads meta['PARAM'] to compute the correct number of blocks. Passing a static tuple grid=(cdiv(N,FIXED_SIZE),...) causes the autotuner to select a config but launch with the wrong grid dimensions, resulting in redundant work or incorrect coverage.
